1 # SaaS Information Architecture — Strict Separation Rules 2 3 **Created:** 2026-04-18, v1.0. 4 **Authority:** Vega (enforces on every design review). pod-a-frontend, pod-b-frontend, pod-c-frontend, pixel ALL load this. 5 **Reason:** Current SaaS builds show the same page in multiple places (sidebar + settings menu). That's amateur-hour IA. Every Boldteq product MUST pass this separation audit before Bolt deploys. 6 7 --- 8 9 ## The 4 navigation surfaces (and what belongs where) 10 11 Every Boldteq SaaS has exactly **4 navigation surfaces**. Each has a strict, non-overlapping scope. A page appears in EXACTLY ONE surface. No duplication. 12 13 ### Surface 1 — Sidebar (primary workspace operations) 14 **What belongs:** The things a user DOES every day inside this workspace. 15 - Dashboard / Overview (landing page after login) 16 - Core domain objects (Resumes, Jobs, Orders, Campaigns, Stores, Projects — whatever the product's nouns are) 17 - Analytics / Reports (about workspace data) 18 - Integrations status (read-only health of connected apps) 19 - Domain-specific workflows (e.g., "Screen candidates", "Run audit", "Build chart") 20 21 **What DOES NOT belong here:** 22 - ❌ Settings (that's Surface 2) 23 - ❌ Account management (that's Surface 3) 24 - ❌ Billing (that's Surface 2 or Surface 3 depending on billing model) 25 - ❌ "Users" or "Team" management (that's Surface 2) 26 - ❌ Help / docs (that's Surface 4) 27 - ❌ Notifications center (that's Surface 4) 28 29 ### Surface 2 — Settings (workspace configuration) 30 **URL pattern:** `/settings/*` or `/w//settings/*` 31 **Entry point:** Gear icon in top bar OR last link in sidebar (NEVER both). 32 **What belongs:** Things about THIS WORKSPACE that you configure occasionally, not daily. 33 34 Standard tabs (in this order): 35 1. **General** — workspace name, logo, default timezone, locale 36 2. **Team** — members, roles, invites, permissions 37 3. **Billing** — plan, invoices, payment method (ONLY if workspace-scoped billing; else see Surface 3) 38 4. **Integrations** — connected apps + API keys + webhooks (configuring; health is Surface 1) 39 5. **Appearance** — theme override, brand colors (if multi-tenant white-label) 40 6. **Advanced** — data export, workspace deletion, danger zone 41 42 ### Surface 3 — Account menu (user-scoped, cross-workspace) 43 **Entry point:** Top-right avatar dropdown. Always. 44 **What belongs:** Things about THE USER, not the workspace. 45 46 Menu items (in this order): 47 1. **Profile** — name, email, avatar, personal timezone 48 2. **Security** — password, 2FA, active sessions, API tokens (user-scoped) 49 3. **Notifications** — email prefs, notification channels (user-scoped) 50 4. **Billing** — ONLY if user-scoped billing (per-seat across workspaces) 51 5. **Divider** 52 6. **Workspace switcher** (see § Agency/Multi-tenant pattern below) 53 7. **Divider** 54 8. **Help & Docs** (links to Surface 4) 55 9. **Sign out** 56 57 ### Surface 4 — Global utilities (top bar, non-menu) 58 - Search (Cmd+K) — global across workspace 59 - Notifications bell — dropdown with unread count 60 - Help (?) — help center + chat 61 - Workspace switcher — when present, top-LEFT not top-right (see pattern below) 62 63 --- 64 65 ## The No-Duplication Rule (enforce on every review) 66 67 A single concept MUST NOT appear in two surfaces. Common mistakes: 68 69 | Concept | WRONG (duplicates) | RIGHT | 70 |---|---|---| 71 | Team members | Sidebar "Users" AND Settings > Team | Only Settings > Team | 72 | Billing | Sidebar "Billing" AND Settings > Billing AND Account > Billing | Only ONE — usually Settings > Billing (workspace-scoped) | 73 | API keys | Sidebar "Developers" AND Settings > Integrations | Only Settings > Integrations (workspace keys) or Account > Security (user tokens) — pick by scope | 74 | Profile | Settings > Profile AND Account > Profile | Only Account > Profile (user-scoped) | 75 | Audit logs | Sidebar "Logs" AND Settings > Audit | Only Settings > Advanced > Audit logs (workspace data, not daily-use) | 76 | Notifications center | Top bar bell AND sidebar "Inbox" | Only top bar bell | 77 78 **Audit script** (Vega runs this before approval): 79 ```bash 80 # Find duplicated route targets in sidebar vs settings vs account menu 81 grep -rE 'href="/[a-z-]+' app/components/sidebar.tsx app/components/settings-nav.tsx app/components/user-menu.tsx \ 82 | awk -F'"' '{print $2}' | sort | uniq -c | awk '$1 > 1' 83 # Expect: empty output (no duplicates) 84 ``` 85 86 --- 87 88 ## Decision tree: where does X live? 89 90 When building a new page, run this check: 91 92 ``` 93 Is it a daily-use workflow action? → Sidebar 94 ↓ no 95 Is it configuring the workspace? → Settings 96 ↓ no 97 Is it about the individual user (cross-workspace)? → Account menu 98 ↓ no 99 Is it a global utility (search/notif/help)? → Top bar 100 ↓ no 101 Reconsider — it probably doesn't belong in navigation at all. Inline link from the relevant page. 102 ``` 103 104 If unsure, the default is **Settings**. Sidebars stay lean. 105 106 --- 107 108 ## Sidebar composition rules 109 110 - **Max items:** 7 primary + divider + 2-3 secondary (e.g., Integrations health, Admin panel link) 111 - **No nesting > 1 level.** If you have submenus, reconsider grouping. 112 - **Dashboard / Overview is ALWAYS the first item.** 113 - **Active state:** `bg-accent text-accent-foreground` (Stack A) or `` (Stack B) 114 - **Group by noun, not verb.** "Resumes" not "Screen Candidates". The action is implicit from the page you land on. 115 116 ### Stack A sidebar reference (shadcn/ui) 117 ```tsx 118 119 120 {/* only if multi-tenant/agency mode */} 121 122 123 124 125 Dashboard 126 Resumes 127 Jobs 128 Analytics 129 130 131 132 133 134 Integrations 135 136 137 138 139 Settings 140 141 142 143 ``` 144 145 --- 146 147 ## Agency / Multi-tenant workspace switcher 148 149 ### When you need it 150 Boldteq products run in 3 modes: 151 152 | Mode | Single workspace | Multi-tenant | Agency | 153 |---|---|---|---| 154 | Who uses | Solo user, one workspace | Users in teams with workspaces | Boldteq partners managing N client workspaces | 155 | Switcher needed? | NO | YES (switch between their workspaces) | YES (switch between client workspaces + agency admin view) | 156 | Default for new Boldteq product | — | — | Multi-tenant unless product-specific reason | 157 158 Rex/Arya set `saas_mode: 'single' | 'multi-tenant' | 'agency'` in the project CLAUDE.md. Pod frontends read this and scaffold the right shell. 159 160 ### Workspace switcher placement 161 **Top-LEFT of the sidebar header.** NOT in the account menu. Reasons: 162 1. Workspace context defines everything on screen — it must be visually anchored with the rest of workspace UX (sidebar) 163 2. Account menu is for user-level actions that span workspaces — switcher changes workspace context, it's not a user action 164 3. Every major SaaS with this pattern places it top-left: Linear, Notion, Slack, Shopify Partners 165 166 ### Switcher component pattern (Stack A) 167 168 ```tsx 169 170 171 172 {current.name} 173 174 175 176 Switch workspace 177 {workspaces.map(w => ( 178 switchTo(w.id)}> 179 180 {w.name} 181 {w.id === current.id && } 182 183 ))} 184 185 }> 186 Create workspace 187 188 {mode === 'agency' && ( 189 }> 190 Agency admin 191 192 )} 193 194 195 ``` 196 197 ### URL structure (REQUIRED for multi-tenant/agency) 198 - `/w//...` — every workspace-scoped URL 199 - `/account/...` — user-scoped (Profile, Security) 200 - `/agency/...` — agency-owner-only (ONLY in agency mode) 201 - `/` → redirect to last visited workspace OR workspace picker if multiple 202 203 Routing middleware (Stack A Next.js): 204 ```ts 205 // middleware.ts — every request 206 // 1. Authenticate user 207 // 2. Resolve workspace slug from URL 208 // 3. Verify user has access to that workspace (membership check) 209 // 4. Inject workspace context into RSC via headers/cookies 210 // 5. 404 if no access 211 ``` 212 213 ### Agency mode — extra surface: Agency admin area 214 **URL:** `/agency/*` 215 **Access:** Only agency owner + agency team roles. Regular workspace members CANNOT see. 216 **Pages:** 217 - `/agency` — overview (total clients, revenue, active users) 218 - `/agency/clients` — list of client workspaces, ability to impersonate, onboard new 219 - `/agency/billing` — consolidated billing (all client subscriptions Boldteq manages) 220 - `/agency/team` — agency team members (not end-client users) 221 - `/agency/white-label` — branding applied across client workspaces 222 - `/agency/reports` — cross-client analytics (with client privacy controls) 223 224 Agency admin is **NOT a workspace.** It's a meta-workspace that manages other workspaces. The switcher includes "Agency admin" as a special top-level entry (see § switcher component). 225 226 --- 227 228 ## Data model implications (for Dato / pod-X-db) 229 230 Multi-tenant + agency modes require: 231 232 ```sql 233 -- Core tables 234 workspaces (id, slug, name, logo_url, owner_user_id, agency_id NULL, plan, created_at) 235 workspace_members (workspace_id, user_id, role enum('owner','admin','member','viewer'), invited_by, joined_at) 236 agencies (id, name, owner_user_id, created_at) 237 agency_clients (agency_id, workspace_id, onboarded_at, is_managed_billing bool) 238 239 -- On every workspace-scoped table, mandatory column: 240 -- workspace_id uuid REFERENCES workspaces(id) NOT NULL 241 -- + index on workspace_id 242 -- + RLS policy: "members of workspace_id can read/write" 243 ``` 244 245 RLS policy template (Stack A Supabase): 246 ```sql 247 CREATE POLICY "workspace_members_all" ON 248 FOR ALL TO authenticated 249 USING ( 250 workspace_id IN ( 251 SELECT workspace_id FROM workspace_members 252 WHERE user_id = auth.uid() 253 ) 254 ); 255 ``` 256 257 Agency admin bypass (carefully scoped): 258 ```sql 259 CREATE POLICY "agency_owner_read" ON
260 FOR SELECT TO authenticated 261 USING ( 262 workspace_id IN ( 263 SELECT ac.workspace_id FROM agency_clients ac 264 JOIN agencies a ON a.id = ac.agency_id 265 WHERE a.owner_user_id = auth.uid() AND ac.is_managed_billing = true 266 ) 267 ); 268 ``` 269 270 --- 271 272 ## Anti-patterns (NEVER do these) 273 274 1. **Never put the same concept in sidebar + settings.** Duplication = user confusion = support tickets. 275 2. **Never put workspace switcher in account menu.** It belongs top-LEFT sidebar header. 276 3. **Never collapse Settings > Team into the sidebar as "Users".** Team management is configuration, not daily work. 277 4. **Never put billing in sidebar.** It's not a daily-use workflow; it's configuration. 278 5. **Never put workspace-scoped features under `/account/`.** Account = user-global. 279 6. **Never omit the workspace slug from URLs in multi-tenant mode.** `/dashboard` is ambiguous; `/w/acme/dashboard` is not. 280 7. **Never let an agency owner see a client workspace's data without explicit impersonation.** Privacy + legal. 281 8. **Never show "Agency admin" in the switcher to non-agency users.** Role-scope the menu. 282 9. **Never ship more than 7 primary sidebar items.** If you need more, reconsider grouping. 283 10. **Never nest sidebar items more than 1 level.** Shallow navigation > deep hierarchy. 284 11. **Never skip RLS on workspace-scoped tables.** P0 tenant leakage risk. 285 12. **Never ship without the audit script passing** (no duplicates in sidebar/settings/account nav). 286 287 --- 288 289 ## Verification (Vega blocks deploy on any fail) 290 291 ```bash 292 # 1. No duplicate href across nav surfaces 293 ./scripts/audit-nav-duplicates.sh # exits 1 on duplicates 294 295 # 2. Workspace slug in all workspace routes 296 grep -rE 'href="/[a-z]' app/ | grep -v '/w/' | grep -v '/account' | grep -v '/agency' 297 # Expect: only landing / auth / /api routes 298 299 # 3. RLS on every workspace-scoped table 300 psql $DATABASE_URL -f scripts/audit-rls.sql 301 # Expect: zero rows returned (all tables with workspace_id have policies) 302 303 # 4. Settings nav items match the standard 6 tabs (General, Team, Billing, Integrations, Appearance, Advanced) 304 grep -oE 'href="/settings/[a-z]+"' app/components/settings-nav.tsx | sort -u 305 # Compare against standard list 306 ``` 307 308 --- 309 310 ## Migration path (for existing products — Rankora, CROBOT) 311 312 Rankora/CROBOT are Stack A (Vite origin). Both likely have duplication (Yash's exact feedback). Migration: 313 314 1. Audit current navigation with `./scripts/audit-nav-duplicates.sh` 315 2. List duplications in a migration doc 316 3. For each duplication: pick the correct surface (per decision tree), remove from the other 317 4. Add workspace switcher if multi-tenant/agency mode applies (Rankora: likely yes; CROBOT: likely yes) 318 5. Reshape URL structure to `/w//...` 319 6. Add RLS policies on any currently-leaky tables 320 7. Deploy behind feature flag; dogfood for 1 week 321 8. Remove old routes 322 323 Assign: koda (Stack A backend), pod-a-frontend (once hired in Cohort 3), dato (RLS), sage (review). Vega approves final shell. 324

10	
11	# InkOS Build Lessons
12	
13	## 1. Recurring Sage Findings — Systematic Pipeline Weaknesses
14	
15	### 1A. RPC Parameter Mismatches (Dato writes RPC, Koda writes route with different params)
16	
17	Appeared in Sprint 5 (C1: camelCase `submissionId` vs snake_case `submission_id` in consent PDF job), Sprint 6 (C1: `public_get_invite_by_token` vs `get_invite_by_token`; C2: `accept_team_invite` missing `artist_id` and `commission_default_pct` in return shape), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), and Sprint 8 (S8#1: `set_artist_tax_info` param mismatch). Root cause: Dato writes the migration defining the RPC signature, Koda writes the API route consuming it, and neither verifies the other's contract. The hand-written `lib/supabase/types.ts` masks the drift because TypeScript trusts whatever is manually typed. **Prevention rule:** Before Koda writes any route that calls an RPC, the RPC's exact parameter names and return fields must be extracted from the migration SQL into a shared TypeScript interface. If Dato and Koda run in parallel, the contract must be defined in the design spec as a shared interface BEFORE either starts coding.
18	
19	### 1B. Column Name Drift (migration says X, types say Y, code says Z)
20	
21	Appeared in Sprint 1 (C3: `locations` migration missing `zip`/`phone` that types declared), Sprint 3 (C2: `sort_order` column missing from migration but code referenced it), Sprint 6 (C3: `studio_members.last_active_at` not in migration but in types), Sprint 7 (M1: `applied_date` vs `applied_at`), Sprint 8-12 audit (S11#8: `status` column on `marketing_campaigns` missing, S12#12: `payroll_items` table referenced but doesn't exist). Root cause: `lib/supabase/types.ts` was hand-edited throughout the build instead of regenerated from the actual DB schema. **Prevention rule:** Never hand-edit the types file. After every Dato migration, run `pnpm supabase gen types typescript --linked > lib/supabase/types.ts`. If the Supabase project doesn't exist yet (as in InkOS), maintain a strict convention: Dato writes the migration, Dato updates types to exactly match, and Koda does NOT touch the types file. Any column referenced in code must exist in the migration first.
22	
23	### 1C. `asChild` Violations on base-nova
24	
25	Every Sage audit checked for `asChild` usage on base-nova (shadcn/ui's `@base-ui-components/react`) components. In InkOS this passed cleanly because it was caught early (Sprint 1 scan), but the automated grep for `asChild` was added to every single audit because this is a known recurring problem across Boldteq builds. **Rule:** All components from base-nova use the `render` prop pattern, never `asChild`. This must be in every project's ESLint config as a custom rule or at minimum in the Sage automated scan.
26	
27	### 1D. Missing Rate Limits on GET Endpoints
28	
29	Sprint 1 (M1: auth rate limits architecturally impossible), Sprint 6 (public invite route needed rate limit), Sprint 8-12 combined audit (cross-sprint #17: payroll GET routes missing rate limits). Koda consistently forgets rate limits on read routes, treating them as "safe." But unbounded GETs enable enumeration, scraping, and DoS. **Rule:** Every API route, GET or POST, must import and call either `authedRatelimit` or `publicBookingReadRatelimit` before any DB query. Sage scans for routes missing rate-limit calls.
30	
31	### 1E. `onValueChange` Null Guards for base-ui Select
32	
33	Not specific to InkOS (passed here) but flagged as a check item in every audit. When base-ui Select fires `onValueChange`, the value can be `null` on deselect. Without a guard, the handler crashes or sends null to the API. **Rule:** Every `onValueChange` handler must check `if (value === null) return` before processing.
34	
35	### 1F. `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` Violations
36	
37	Sprint 4 build report (item #2): interface optionals needed `| undefined` suffix. Throughout the build, Koda hit TypeScript errors where `{ field?: string }` doesn't accept `undefined` under strict optional property types. **Rule:** Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, always declare optional fields as `field?: string | undefined` in interfaces. Or better: use Zod schema inference (`z.infer<typeof Schema>`) which handles this automatically.
38	
39	### 1G. Feature Gate Key Mismatches
40	
41	Sprint 7 (C1): the plans JSONB in the billing migration used `commission_splits` but all code used `commissions`. Today's static `requireFeature()` compares plan order (not JSONB keys), so it accidentally worked. But if anyone switches to the RPC-based `requireFeatureRpc()` (which reads JSONB), all gates 403. **Rule:** Define all feature gate keys in a single `lib/billing/feature-keys.ts` constant. Both the migration seed data and the `requireFeature()` callers import from this file. Drift is a compile error instead of a runtime surprise.
42	
43	### 1H. Public Routes Using Session Client Instead of Anon
44	
45	Sprint 5 (C6, C7): public consent pages imported `createClient` from `@/lib/supabase/server` (session-cookie client) instead of `createPublicClient`. Functional today (RPC grants to anon) but leaks the logged-in user's session into a public route. **Rule:** Every route under `/book/`, `/consent/`, `/invite/`, or `/api/public/` must use `createPublicClient()` from `@/lib/supabase/public`. Sage grepping for `createClient` in public routes is now a mandatory scan.
46	
47	### 1I. `unstable_cache` Capturing Authenticated Clients
48	
49	Sprint 7 (M3): `unstable_cache(async () => supabase.rpc(...))` captured the first caller's authenticated client. Subsequent requests within the cache TTL reuse the first caller's JWT. **Rule:** Never wrap `supabase.rpc()` calls in `unstable_cache` when the supabase client is session-scoped. Cache the RESULT of the RPC call (a plain object), not the client invocation. Or just don't use `unstable_cache` for authenticated data -- it's not worth the footgun.
50	
51	## 2. Sprint Velocity Patterns — What Worked for Parallel Execution
52	
53	### 2A. Dato + Vega in Parallel (No Dependency)
54	
55	Dato writes the migration (schema, RPCs, RLS, triggers) while Vega writes the design spec (UI layout, component hierarchy, interaction patterns). These have zero dependencies. Starting them in parallel saves 2-4 hours per sprint. Koda then consumes BOTH outputs to build the API routes and UI.
56	
57	### 2B. Sage Audit in Background While Next Sprint Starts
58	
59	After Koda delivers a sprint, Sage audits the output while Dato and Vega start on the next sprint. The next sprint's Koda build can begin on features that don't overlap with the audit scope. This pipeline parallelism was critical for shipping 13 sprints in 2 days. Exception: if Sage's audit is BLOCK severity, the fix Koda must run before proceeding.
60	
61	### 2C. Fix Koda + Build Koda Can Run in Parallel If File Scopes Don't Overlap
62	
63	When Sage flags fixes in Sprint N, a "fix Koda" agent addresses those while a "build Koda" agent starts Sprint N+1's non-overlapping files. This worked well when Sprint 3 fixes (client CRM) ran alongside Sprint 4 scaffold (billing). Does NOT work when the fix touches shared infrastructure like `lib/supabase/types.ts` or `lib/supabase/server.ts`.
64	
65	### 2D. API 500 Errors Recovered by Checking Partial State
66	
67	When a sprint's build partially failed (e.g., missing column caused a 500), Rex dispatched a fix agent that first checked what was already built and correct, then surgically fixed only the broken parts. Avoids the temptation to rewrite entire files.
68	
69	### 2E. Batch Sage Audits Are Worse Than Per-Sprint Audits
70	
71	Sprints 8-12 were batched into one combined Sage audit. This found 4 critical issues that had been compounding for 5 sprints. Per-sprint audits (Sprints 1-7) caught issues immediately, before they could cascade. **Rule:** Run Sage after EVERY sprint, not batched. The 30-minute audit cost per sprint is cheaper than the 4-hour compound fix session.
72	
73	## 3. Architecture Decisions That Proved Right
74	
75	### 3A. RPC-Only Writes for Audit-Critical Tables
76	
77	`consent_form_submissions` has zero direct-write RLS policies -- all writes go through `submit_consent_form` RPC. `commission_records` same pattern. This means: (a) business logic (snapshot creation, audit hash, penalty generation) can't be bypassed; (b) the RPC is the single source of truth for mutation semantics; (c) RLS stays simple (just read policies). **Apply to:** Any table where data integrity is a legal or financial obligation (consent, pay, billing, audit logs).
78	
79	### 3B. `EXCLUDE USING gist` for Booking Conflicts
80	
81	The `bookings_artist_no_overlap` exclusion constraint catches double-bookings at the DB level. Every write path (API route, public RPC, admin override) that creates/moves a booking is automatically protected. Without this, every write path would need its own conflict-check query, and one would inevitably be missed. Effort to set up: 5 lines of SQL. Effort saved: hours of bug-hunting. **Apply to:** Any domain with time-range conflicts (schedules, reservations, resource allocation).
82	
83	### 3C. `GENERATED ALWAYS` Columns for Computed Values
84	
85	`bookings.end_at` is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (scheduled_at + (duration_min || ' minutes')::interval) STORED`. This means `end_at` can never drift from `scheduled_at + duration`. No code path can accidentally set a wrong `end_at`. Sage verified this by grepping for `end_at` in INSERT/UPDATE payloads -- zero hits. **Apply to:** Any column that's a deterministic function of other columns (totals, dates, durations).
86	
87	### 3D. Feature Gate Server-Enforced + UI-Hidden (Dual Enforcement)
88	
89	Every gated feature has: (1) `requireFeature(plan, 'key')` in the API route that returns 403, AND (2) `featureKey` in the sidebar nav-config that hides the link AND (3) `<UpgradeGate>` component that shows a blur overlay. Three layers means a user can never reach a paid feature through URL manipulation, deep linking, or API probing. **Apply to:** Every SaaS with tiered plans.
90	
91	### 3E. Worker-Only for Expensive Operations
92	
93	AI design generation (Claude + DALL-E pipeline), PDF generation (react-pdf/renderer), and low-stock email alerts all run in BullMQ workers, never in API routes. This prevents: request timeouts, memory pressure on the web process, and blocking other requests. **Apply to:** Any operation that takes >5s or uses >100MB memory.
94	
95	## 4. Architecture Decisions That Caused Problems
96	
97	### 4A. Hand-Written `lib/supabase/types.ts`
98	
99	This was the single largest source of bugs across the entire build. Every sprint had at least one finding traceable to types not matching the migration. The types file was 3000+ lines of manually maintained TypeScript that drifted from reality. **Fix for future builds:** Use `pnpm supabase gen types typescript` after every migration. If the Supabase project doesn't exist yet, use `supabase start` locally and generate from the local DB. Never hand-edit.
100	
101	### 4B. Sprint 2 Availability RPC Stubbed Then Replaced
102	
103	`public_get_availability` was stubbed in Sprint 2, then substantially rewritten in Sprint 6 when artist schedules landed. The Sprint 2 version returned mock data; callers assumed it was real. When Sprint 6 replaced it, the return shape changed and broke the public booking flow silently (fields were guarded by `&&` checks, so they just disappeared). **Rule:** Stubs must return the EXACT shape of the final implementation (even if values are empty/default). Document which fields are stubbed vs real.
104	
105	### 4C. `proxy.ts` vs `middleware.ts` in Next 16
106	
107	Next.js 16 renamed the middleware entrypoint from `middleware.ts` to `proxy.ts`. Every reference to "middleware" in docs, comments, and design specs was wrong. The actual `proxy.ts` file existed and worked, but new contributors would look for `middleware.ts` and not find it. **Rule:** On every Next.js major version, verify the middleware filename convention. Document it in the project CLAUDE.md.
108	
109	## 5. Koda Recurring Type Fix Patterns
110	
111	### 5A. `Object.assign` Bypass for Supabase `RejectExcessProperties`
112	
113	When Supabase client's `.update()` or `.insert()` rejects unknown properties, Koda used `Object.assign(base, { extra_field: value })` to sneak in properties not in the TypeScript type. Sprint 3 (C2): this was used to write a `sort_order` column that didn't exist. The `Object.assign` defeated TypeScript's protection and the write silently no-oped. **Rule:** NEVER use `Object.assign` to build Supabase mutation payloads. If a field isn't in the type, it shouldn't be in the mutation. If it SHOULD be there, fix the type first.
114	
115	### 5B. `unknown as TableInsert` Cast Pattern
116	
117	When the Supabase generated types don't match what code needs to insert, Koda cast `payload as unknown as Database['public']['Tables']['x']['Insert']`. This bypasses all type checking. Acceptable ONLY when the mismatch is between the generated type and the actual DB schema (which happens when types aren't regenerated). **Rule:** Fix the root cause (regenerate types) instead of casting.
118	
119	### 5C. `Resolver<FormValues>` Explicit Cast for react-hook-form
120	
121	react-hook-form's `zodResolver()` returns a type that doesn't exactly match `Resolver<T>` under strict settings. Koda added explicit `as Resolver<FormValues>` casts. This is a known library typing issue and the cast is safe. **Rule:** Acceptable -- document in codebase as a known workaround.
122	
123	### 5D. `render` Not `asChild` on Every base-nova Component
124	
125	Covered in 1C above. Every component from `@base-ui-components/react` uses `render` prop, never `asChild`. Koda initially used `asChild` (Radix habit), caught in Sprint 1, never repeated.
126	
127	### 5E. `.slice(0, 10)` Instead of `.split('T')[0]` for ISO Date Extraction
128	
129	Under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `.split('T')[0]` returns `string | undefined` because TypeScript doesn't know the array has a first element. `.slice(0, 10)` returns `string` always. **Rule:** For extracting the date portion of an ISO string, use `.slice(0, 10)`. It's type-safe and doesn't require a non-null assertion.
130	
131	## 6. Dodo Payments Integration Gotchas
132	
133	### 6A. `standardwebhooks` Spec (Not Plain HMAC)
134	
135	Sprint 4 (C1): Dodo webhooks use the `standardwebhooks` library, NOT a plain HMAC. The signing payload is `${webhook-id}.${webhook-timestamp}.${rawBody}`, the secret is base64-decoded (strip `whsec_` prefix), and the signature header format is `v1,base64sig`. A plain `createHmac('sha256', secret).update(rawBody).digest('hex')` will NEVER match. **Rule:** Use `import { Webhook } from 'standardwebhooks'` and call `wh.verify(rawBody, headers)`. The idempotency key is the `webhook-id` header, not a body-level `event_id` field (which Dodo doesn't send).
136	
137	### 6B. `customer: {customer_id}` Object Format
138	
139	Dodo SDK v2 `subscriptions.create` and `payments.create` take `customer: CustomerRequest` object (with `customer_id` field inside), NOT a top-level `customer_id` string. **Rule:** Always wrap: `{ customer: { customer_id: dodoCustomerId } }`.
140	
141	### 6C. `billing: {country}` Required on Checkout
142	
143	Every Dodo checkout call requires a `billing: { country: 'US' }` field. Without it, the API returns a 400 that's hard to debug. **Rule:** Always include `billing: { country }` in checkout creation.
144	
145	### 6D. `return_url` Not `success_url/cancel_url`
146	
147	Dodo uses a single `return_url` for post-checkout redirect, not separate `success_url` and `cancel_url` like Stripe. **Rule:** Pass `return_url` pointing to a confirmation page that checks the subscription/payment status.
148	
149	### 6E. Portal Method Returns `{link}`
150	
151	`dodo.customers.customerPortal.create(customerId, { return_url })` returns `{ link: string }`, not a full URL string. Access via `result.link`. **Rule:** Destructure: `const { link } = await dodo.customers.customerPortal.create(...)`.
152	
153	### 6F. Lazy Proxy Init for SDK Client
154	
155	Both `lib/dodo/client.ts` and `lib/queue.ts` were constructing SDK clients at module evaluation time. During `pnpm build`, env vars aren't available, causing a crash. Fixed with a lazy proxy pattern that defers construction until first use. **Rule:** Any SDK client that reads env vars at construction time must use lazy initialization. Pattern:
156	
157	```ts
158	let _client: DodoPayments | null = null
159	function getClient(): DodoPayments {
160	  if (!_client) _client = new DodoPayments({ token: process.env.DODO_API_KEY! })
161	  return _client
162	}
163	```
164	
165	## 7. What to Do Differently Next Time
166	
167	### 7A. Generate Types from DB Immediately
168	
169	The hand-written types file caused the highest density of bugs in this build. Next project: `supabase start` locally on day 1, run `supabase gen types` after every migration, commit the generated file. If using a remote Supabase project, generate from that. Zero hand-editing of the types file.
170	
171	### 7B. Run Sage After Every Sprint, Not Batched
172	
173	Sprints 1-7 each got individual Sage audits. Sprints 8-12 were batched into one audit. The batch audit found 4 CRITICAL issues that had been compounding for 5 sprints. Individual audits would have caught each issue in the sprint that introduced it, when the fix is 15 minutes instead of 2 hours. **Rule:** Sage audit is a mandatory step between sprints, not optional or batchable.
174	
175	### 7C. Define RPC Contracts as Shared TypeScript Interfaces BEFORE Dato Writes Migration
176	
177	The #1 integration bug category (1A above) is Dato and Koda disagreeing on RPC parameter names and return shapes. Fix: in the design spec, define each RPC as a TypeScript interface:
178	
179	```ts
180	// Sprint 5 design spec would include:
181	interface SubmitConsentFormParams {
182	  p_studio_id: string
183	  p_template_id: string
184	  p_submission_data: Json
185	  // ... exact param names that Dato will use in CREATE FUNCTION
186	}
187	interface SubmitConsentFormReturn {
188	  submission_id: string
189	  consent_token: string
190	  // ... exact fields that Koda will read
191	}
192	```
193	
194	Dato implements the SQL to match. Koda implements the route to match. Mismatch is impossible because both reference the same spec.
195	
196	### 7D. Create `.env.local.template` That Can Be Copied in One Command
197	
198	InkOS accumulated 30+ env vars across 13 sprints. Each new env var was mentioned in a build report but not collected in one place until late. **Rule:** Maintain a `.env.local.template` from Sprint 0 that's updated every sprint. New developer setup: `cp .env.local.template .env.local` then fill in secrets.
199	
200	### 7E. Storage RLS Must Be Checked Per-Bucket, Per-Sprint
201	
202	Sprint 1 fixed storage RLS for `studio-assets`. Sprint 2 added `design-assets` bucket without copying the RLS pattern. Sprint 2 Sage caught it. Sprint 5 added `consent-forms` bucket -- same risk. **Rule:** Every time a Dato migration creates a new storage bucket, Sage must verify that SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies exist with folder-prefix tenant checks. Add to the automated scan.
203	
204	### 7F. Admin Routes Must Use Service-Role Client After Platform Admin Gate
205	
206	Sprint 4 (C2): All admin billing routes used the session client, so RLS restricted the platform admin to their own studio's data. Admin routes see zero cross-tenant data. **Rule:** After verifying `is_platform_admin`, switch to `createServiceRoleClient()`. The admin gate is authorization; service-role bypasses RLS for the cross-tenant query.
207	
208	### 7G. CSV/Export Routes Must Sanitize for Formula Injection
209	
210	Sprint 3 (C3): `Papa.unparse` does not escape cells starting with `= + - @ \t \r`. Any export feature is a CWE-1236 vector. **Rule:** Every CSV export must wrap cell values in a `sanitiseCsvCell()` function that prefixes dangerous characters with `'`. Add this to the shared `lib/utils.ts` in the starter template.
211	
212	### 7H. Delete Operations Must Verify Affected Row Count
213	
214	Sprint 3 (M2): Supabase `.delete()` returns `{ error: null }` even when RLS denies the delete (zero rows affected). The UI optimistically removes the item, but on reload it's back. **Rule:** Always use `.delete({ count: 'exact' })` and check `count === 0` to return 403/404. Apply to every DELETE handler.
215	
216	### 7I. Mutation Routes Must Use RPCs When RPCs Exist
217	
218	Sprint 6 (M2): Dato wrote `change_member_role` and `deactivate_member` RPCs with last-owner protection and audit logging. Koda's API routes bypassed them with direct `.update()` calls, losing all the safety logic. **Rule:** If a SECURITY DEFINER RPC exists for a mutation, the API route MUST call it. Direct `.update()` or `.insert()` bypasses triggers, audit logging, and business rules baked into the RPC.

2	
3	Every Boldteq SaaS must ship with a comprehensive admin panel. This standard consolidates patterns from Stripe, Shopify, Vercel, Linear, and the project, combined with SOC 2, GDPR, and security best practices.

11	## Part 1: Architecture & Information Hierarchy
12	
13	### Admin Panel Structure
14	
15	Single-page application at `/admin` with sidebar navigation and tab-based content. Each tab is isolated with its own error boundary so one tab crashing doesn't kill the whole admin.
16	
17	```
18	Admin.tsx (state: activeSection)
19	├── AdminHeader (top nav: org logo, Cmd+K palette, account menu)
20	├── AdminSidebar (left nav: grouped sections, active indicator, collapsible sub-items)
21	├── AdminErrorBoundary key={activeSection}
22	│   └── sectionComponents[activeSection] (dynamic render)
23	```

27	**Modern pattern (2025):**
28	- **Level 1:** Top-level sections (Dashboard, Users, Billing, Settings, System)
29	- **Level 2:** Sub-items within sections (e.g., under Settings: Configuration, Feature Flags, SEO, Audit Logs)
30	- **Keyboard:** Cmd+K or Ctrl+K opens command palette for jump navigation

136	## Part 2: Mandatory Admin Tabs (Enhanced)

138	### 1. Dashboard — Overview Tab
139	
140	**Purpose:** At-a-glance platform health and key metrics.
141	
142	**Layout Pattern (Progressive Disclosure):**
143	- High-level KPIs in large cards (top row)
144	- Charts/trends below (date range picker)
145	- Recent activity / alerts lower
146	- Don't overwhelm with 20+ widgets — focus on 4-6 key metrics
147	
148	**Required KPIs (customize by product):**
149	- Total active users (with 7d/30d growth %)
150	- Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) if subscription-based, or total revenue
151	- Key product metric (jobs ranked for the project, orders for e-commerce, messages for chat)
152	- System health (uptime %, error rate, latency p95)
153	
154	**Required charts:**
155	- User signups over time (30-day rolling window)
156	- Revenue/usage trend (30-day rolling)
157	- Critical alerts or issues count
158	- All charts must have date range picker (last 7/30/90 days, custom)
159	
160	**Data pattern:**
161	- Dashboard data comes from edge function or RPC aggregating from multiple tables
162	- Real-time updates: use Supabase real-time subscriptions for status indicators (uptime, error rates)
163	- Batch updates acceptable for historical trends (daily snapshots)
164	
165	**Implementation note:**
166	- Skeleton loaders while data loads
167	- Empty state if no data (explains why — "only 2 days of data available")

588	  const { data: { user: admin } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();

1299	### Dark Patterns to Avoid (20+ Common Mistakes)
1300	
1301	1. **Missing audit logs** — No record of who deleted what when. Fail SOC 2.
1302	2. **No confirmation dialogs** — User clicks delete twice, whole dataset gone.
1303	3. **Hardcoded admin checks** — e.g., `if (email === 'admin@company.com') { allow }`. Impossible to manage multiple admins.
1304	4. **No pagination** — Try to load 1M rows into a table. Browser crashes.
1305	5. **Client-side only search** — Search by loading all data, filtering in JS. Slow + insecure.
1306	6. **Missing loading states** — Table appears blank while loading. User thinks it's broken.
1307	7. **No error boundaries** — One tab crash kills entire admin panel.
1308	8. **PII exposed in URLs** — Admin URLs show user emails or IDs in plaintext query params.
1309	9. **No rate limiting** — Attacker can bulk-create 1000 users per second.
1310	10. **Destructive actions too easy** — Delete button same size as other buttons, no confirmation.
1311	11. **No GDPR export workflow** — User asks for data. Admin manually emails them a file.
1312	12. **No data retention policy** — Audit logs kept forever (storage bloat, privacy risk).
1313	13. **Session never expires** — Admin logs in, leaves laptop at desk, anyone can access admin panel.
1314	14. **No MFA requirement** — Admin password compromised = entire app compromised.
1315	15. **Hover-to-reveal actions** — Edit/delete buttons only show on hover. Inaccessible to keyboard users.
1316	16. **Color-only status indicators** — Red = error? Warning? Pending? Users with color blindness confused.
1317	17. **No empty states** — Blank table with no message. User doesn't know if data is loading or missing.
1318	18. **Slow performance** — Admin clicks edit, waits 5 seconds for form to load.
1319	19. **Inconsistent design** — Different sections look different. Feels like different products.
1320	20. **No user impersonation audit** — Admin "logs in as" user, makes purchases, no record of who did it.
